title: Whitehorse Home Rebates 2026: Heat Pumps Up to $24,000
desc: Whitehorse home rebates for 2026: the Affordable Heat Pump Program covers up to $24,000 and many households may be under its income lines. Where to apply in Whitehorse and what the Dependable Grid pays.
badge: Up to $24,000 for a heat pump
lead: Whitehorse has the territory's main Energy Branch office and a lot of mobile homes. The Affordable Heat Pump Program's income lines are high: for a household of four, after-tax income under $163,300. With a median household total income of $112,000 in 2020, many Whitehorse owners may be worth checking. Here is what is open on October 21, 2026.
cards_heading: What is open for Whitehorse homes in 2026
cards_intro: We read the Government of Yukon pages on October 21, 2026. Each card shows the date and links to the source.

cards.title: Heat pump (lower income)
cards.note: After-tax income under $53,820 for 1 resident, $163,300 for 4. Approval before installing.

cards.title: Heat pump
cards.note: Cold climate air source or ENERGY STAR ground source. Home 6 months or older.

cards.title: Insulation and air sealing
cards.note: Energy assessment first. Air sealing $5,000. Home 5 years or older.

cards.title: Windows
cards.note: Complete ENERGY STAR windows in a building 5 years or older.

cards.title: Non-electric heating
cards.note: Dependable Grid. Existing homes with electric heat.

cards.title: Wood heat
cards.note: EPA-listed stove, boiler, insert, furnace or pellet stove.

sections:
The 2021 Census counted 11,435 households in Whitehorse.

  • Owners. 68% own and 32% rent.
  • Houses and mobile homes. 5,535 households (48%) live in single-detached houses and 1,130 (10%) in movable dwellings.
  • Age. 4,370 homes (38%) were built before 1981, and 1,060 (9%) needed major repairs.

The median household total income was $112,000 in 2020, before tax, and about 17% of households earned under $50,000. The program's own test uses after-tax income for every adult, so use these numbers only as a guide.

The Energy Branch is on the 2nd floor of 4114 4th Avenue, in the RBC Building, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. You can also email energy@yukon.ca or phone 867-393-7063, toll-free in the Yukon 1-800-661-0408, and ask to be transferred. They can talk through a heating change before you commit, which matters because a new system may mean an electrical panel upgrade, a new pole or transformer, an oil tank or propane tank rental, or cutting and storing firewood.

The Affordable Heat Pump Program covers 100% of a project up to $24,000, including the heat pump, electrical upgrades, integration with your current heating and required controls. You must own the home, live in it, and the home must be at least 6 months old. Get approval before you install. After-tax household income must be under $53,820 for one resident, $110,400 for two, $139,150 for three, $163,300 for four and $184,000 for five or more. The income is line 23600 minus line 43500 on the Notice of Assessment of every adult. You must keep your existing heat as a backup, and electric-heated homes must enrol in Yukon Energy's Peak Smart Home program. Households that heat with oil receive an upfront $250 from Natural Resources Canada.
If you are over the income line

You can still claim 50% of project costs up to $10,500 for an air-source heat pump on NRCan's cold climate list for Manitoba and Yukon, or an ENERGY STAR ground-source heat pump. If your home has electric heat, the Dependable Grid dual fuel rebate pays 50% up to $15,000 for a heat pump plus a non-electric backup that keeps running in a power outage. ENERGY STAR windows pay $120 each up to $1,800. Insulation pays up to $12,000 for above-ground walls and $2,500 for an attic, after an energy assessment. We could not tell from Yukon's pages whether mobile homes qualify for each program, so ask the Energy Branch before you plan around it.

Ottawa's National Heat Pump Rebate is expected in early 2027. Yukon's program asks you to disclose NRCan Oil to Heat Pump Affordability funding, and says you cannot use the income-based program if you received it. How the new federal rebate will combine with Yukon's is not published. See our National Heat Pump Rebate guide.
claim_steps: Check your after-tax household income against the Affordable Heat Pump Program limits.
Call or visit the Energy Branch at 4114 4th Avenue before you commit.
Get approval before installing a heat pump under the income-based program.
Keep your existing heating as a backup.
Apply for the rebate with invoices, proof of payment and the electrical inspection report.
faq: Where do I apply for a Yukon rebate in Whitehorse?
You can apply online or use the application form to apply by mail or in person. The Energy Branch is at 4114 4th Avenue, RBC Building, Whitehorse, or phone 867-393-7063.
What is the income limit for a family of four in Whitehorse?
After-tax household income under $163,300 for the Affordable Heat Pump Program, which covers 100% of the project up to $24,000.
Do I need to keep my old heating system?
Yes. Homes with a non-electric system must keep it as backup, and electric-heated homes must keep it and be enrolled in Yukon Energy's Peak Smart Home program.
How long does a Yukon rebate take?
Cheques or e-transfers for the heat pump, window and wood heating rebates arrive within 12 weeks.
Does Whitehorse have its own home energy rebate?
We found no City of Whitehorse home energy rebate on Yukon's pages. The money comes from the Government of Yukon.
